efile.text: The withholding report, as well as the withholding tax returns and any withholding statements required to be submitted to the Department, are all now required to be submitted electronically.

epay.text: TRD-41414 is mandated for electronic filing of tax return and electronic payment of taxes due. The following electronic methods of remitting tax payments will be accepted: credit card, ACH Debit and ACH Credit.

returns.name: Form TRD-41414, Wage Withholding Tax Return
contents: Due on or before the 25th of the month following the end of the tax period; monthly, quarterly or semiannual per the registration certificate; a return (even a zero return) is required for every period.
Filed through TAP (tap.state.nm.us); a paper return is allowed only with an e-file exception or waiver; non-wage withholding is a separate return, TRD-41409.

returns.name: TRD-41431, Workers Compensation Fee Return and Employees Quarterly Wage and Withholding Report
contents: From the quarter beginning January 1, 2026 (House Bill 218) every employer reports each employee's gross wages, pensions or annuity payments and the state income tax withheld; due the 25th of the month after the quarter, electronically.
It carries the workers' compensation fee return (formerly the WC-1) and the per-employee data Section 7-3-13 NMSA 1978 requires; it is filed in addition to the withholding tax returns.
Reporting to the Department of Workforce Solutions or the Workers' Compensation Administration does not satisfy the obligation to report and pay withholding tax.

returns.name: Annual withholding statements (W-2, W-2G, 1042-S, 1099-R)
contents: Filed electronically on or before the last day of January for each employee, pension recipient or winner, through the Combined Federal/State Filing Program or TAP; any federal statement that shows the New Mexico income and withholding is accepted.
Details are in Publication FYI-330, Income and Withholding Information Returns and Filing Methods (not read).

notModelled: Seasonal, temporary and special event filers' monthly periods (the instructions' table).
The annual statements' date: the FYI-104 (11/2025) says the last day of January, the Department's withholding page says the last day of February; the earlier date is recorded.

deposits.interpretation: New Mexico assigns a MONTHLY, QUARTERLY or SEMIANNUAL filing status, shown on the employer's registration certificate (seasonal, temporary and special event filers use monthly), so the frequency is an INPUT and is never derived. Each Form TRD-41414 is due on or before the 25th of the month following the end of the tax period: monthly, the 25th of the next month; quarterly, the 25th of the month after the quarter (April 25, July 25, October 25, January 25); semiannual, January-June due July 25 and July-December due January 25. A due date on a weekend, or a legal, state or national holiday, moves to the next business day. Filing and payment are electronic (credit card, ACH debit and ACH credit); an e-file exception or waiver can be requested. TRD-41414 is a separate return from the quarterly TRD-41431 wage and withholding report.

channels.function: withholding tax returns (TRD-41414, TRD-41409), quarterly wage and withholding report (TRD-41431), annual statements
channels.description: New Mexico Taxpayer Access Point (tap.state.nm.us); the Combined Federal/State Filing Program accepts annual statements
enrollment: Register for a New Mexico Business Tax Identification Number (NMBTIN) with Form ACD-31015, Business Tax Registration Application and Update Form; the reporting obligation continues until the NMBTIN is cancelled.
File all returns, the quarterly report and annual statements electronically through TAP.

returns.name: Employer's Quarterly Wage and Contribution Report (ES-903)
contents: Filed electronically on or before the last day of the month after the quarter (April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31); a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday moves it to the next department business day.
A report is required even when no wages were paid or no tax is due, unless the employer's liability has been terminated or suspended (NMSA 51-1-18).
